component.name: org.nuxeo.agentic.connectors
component.documentation:
Connectors to systems of record: live data from another system on a record page.
A kit's package contributes a connector here, and its component requires org.nuxeo.agentic.connectors. The Connector.Read operation then reads one record through it, for a document the user may read, and returns only the fields the connector allows. The client names the connector and the document, and nothing else.
What each server sets, never a contribution, a document, a layout or the client: the system's address, in the server property the connector's address element names, https only unless nuxeo.agentic.connectors.(the connector's id).http.allowed is true; and its credential, in the server property or the environment variable its credential element names.

extension-point.name: connectors
extension-point.documentation:
One connector per element. Only id, at least one type, address, path, key and at least one field are required. The server properties it names are its own, under nuxeo.agentic.connectors. then its id and a dot, and an environment variable starts NUXEO_CONNECTOR_.
Claim
/claims/{key}
Read
2000 5000 262144 8
The path is appended to the address, with the document's key, one path segment, in place of the key placeholder. The timeouts are in milliseconds, up to 10000 to connect and 30000 for the whole call; maxBytes is up to 1048576, and maxConcurrent, the calls running at once, up to 64. The key is read only from documents of its types. A field's pointer is a JSON pointer into the system's answer, its name by default; only a text, a number or a boolean there is returned. A connector that fails a check is not registered, and the log says why. A later contribution with the same id replaces it whole, and enabled="false" removes it.
